findings.title: Stale denial cache takes precedence over fresher permission cache
findings.body: Check returns a cached denial before consulting permCache, and no code invalidates permDenialCache when fresh permissions are loaded (for example by List calling getIdentityPermissions and repopulating permCache). If a user is denied, is then granted access, and any path refreshes permCache with the new grant, Check for the same namespace/user/action/name/parent still returns Allowed:false until the denial TTL expires. This can make List show a resource while Check denies it and reintroduces up to 30s of stale denial for permission grants.

findings.title: Denials caused by a stale folder tree are cached as authoritative denials
findings.body: When the fresh-permission check fails, Check unconditionally writes permDenialCache. checkPermission/checkInheritedPermissions can fail solely because buildFolderTree returned the 30s-cached folder tree that does not yet contain a newly created or moved parent folder. Such a transient, infrastructure-staleness denial is then stored under the denial key and short-circuits later checks even after the folder tree and permissions have refreshed, extending incorrect denial and undermining the stated goal of letting creators access newly created folders/dashboards promptly in inherited-permission cases.

findings.title: List still trusts stale cached permissions and never re-queries on outdated cache
findings.body: Unlike Check, List returns listPermission directly from getCachedIdentityPermissions whenever a permCache entry exists, regardless of whether that entry predates a newly created dashboard/folder or a new grant. Because the client-side cache was removed in this PR, callers will reach this server List more often but can still omit newly accessible resources for the full shortCacheTTL (30s). The PR goal of fetching newly created dashboards/folders therefore remains broken for list/fetch flows that rely on List rather than a single Check.

findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous underscore-concatenation of variable fields
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates namespace, userUID, action, name and parent with '_' separators and no escaping or length encoding. Distinct tuples can produce the same key, e.g. name='a_b', parent='c' versus name='a', parent='b_c' (UIDs may contain underscores). A denial recorded for one dashboard/folder can therefore incorrectly deny a different resource for the denial TTL.

findings.title: Every cached non-allow now triggers a full database permission load
findings.body: If cached permissions do not allow the request, Check always calls getIdentityPermissions, which reloads identifiers/basic role/teams (subject to their caches) and queries the permission store and rewrites permCache. The denial cache only helps exact repeats of the same action/name/parent; probing or legitimately checking many distinct resources a user cannot access bypasses it and amplifies each check into a DB query. This removes the negative-case protection previously provided by permCache and creates an easy DB load path via enumeration of resource UIDs.
